sections.overview: This pimelodid catfish is native to northwestern South America.
sections.identification: Its tail is deeply forked, with the longest outer rays forming sharply pointed lobes.
sections.habitat: It inhabits freshwater basins including Lake Maracaibo and the Magdalena, Cauca and Sinú rivers.
sections.diet: It feeds on small fishes, crustaceans, worms and other bottom-dwelling animals.
sections.behavior: It is mainly nocturnal and shelters under vegetation or submerged logs by day.
sections.reproduction: In the middle Magdalena basin, it reproduces during the low-water period.
sections.ecology: Unlike S. lima, it has sharply pointed rather than rounded caudal-fin lobes.
sections.conservation: A Cauca River study reports declining populations associated with overfishing and other human impacts.
